It signifies excellence, virtue, or nobility, and is often associated with strong, courageous, and compassionate women in Christian history.

Its association with the color brown likely influenced the naming choice, as darker skin tones and hair colors were common in the European population during that era. The name may also carry connotations of earthiness, stability, and warmth due to its connection with the natural color of the earth.
